parsed.basis: Logar is a largely rural, conservative province southeast of Kabul where foreign visitors are rare and movement through checkpoints and small communities makes anonymity difficult. Under Taliban rule there is no legal recognition or protection for gender identity, while same-sex conduct is punishable by death under Sharia-based provisions and morality officials enforce surveillance of gender and sexual conduct. Documented enforcement nationally includes arbitrary detention, beatings, sexual abuse in custody, public flogging and mob and family violence, with visibly transgender people facing the gravest risks. There is no functioning recourse, protective policing, or gender-affirming care. Discovery in Logar would therefore expose a visitor to detention, corporal or capital punishment, and violence with impunity.
